title: New Flavors and the Rewards Code
lessons: The player sees Black Cherry, Peach, and Dragonberry added to the classic ZYN lineup at retail.
The player peels back the bottom label of a can and finds a Rewards code.

text: Behind the counter, next to the mint and coffee tins you know, there are three new ones. Black Cherry. Peach. Dragonberry.

entry-first-1.speaker: PLAYER
text: Those are new.

entry-first-2.speaker: COUNSEL
text: Black Cherry, Peach, and Dragonberry. Permanent additions, three and six milligrams. Sold at retail nationwide and online through Nicokick. That is the entire announcement. I did not shorten it.

entry-first-3.speaker: PLAYER
text: That sounded like a shelf tag filed an affidavit.

entry-first-4.speaker: COUNSEL
text: The shelf tag was unavailable for comment.

choice-first.speaker: COUNSEL
text: The cashier is waiting. So am I, in a professional capacity.

choices.text: I like having something besides mint, coffee, or cinnamon.
Three fruit flavors feels like expansion for the sake of expansion.
Fruit flavors make me more uncomfortable with nicotine marketing, not less.

first-1.speaker: COUNSEL
text: Noted. Variety is the stated benefit. I have nothing to add, which is unusual for me.

first-2.speaker: COUNSEL
text: They are permanent, not seasonal. So this is the lineup getting bigger, not a test. You may draw your own conclusion about why.

first-2-1.speaker: PLAYER
text: Thank you for making my suspicion sound more expensive.

first-2-2.speaker: COUNSEL
text: Precision is not priced separately.

first-3.speaker: COUNSEL
text: Your concern is noted. The products are restricted to current nicotine users twenty-one and over. That restriction does not require you to like the flavors. I would not ask you to.
At home, you notice the bottom label on the tin peels back. There is a code under it.

entry-return-1.speaker: PLAYER
text: Why am I removing part of the label?

entry-return-2.speaker: COUNSEL
text: There is a code printed under it, on marked cans. You were not meant to find it by accident, but you were meant to find it.

entry-return-3.speaker: PLAYER
text: And then?

entry-return-4.speaker: COUNSEL
text: Fifteen points per code, up to sixty codes a month. Points buy merchandise, gift cards, gear, or experiences, while supplies last, subject to the program terms. I have read the program terms.

entry-return-5.speaker: PLAYER
text: So the can has homework.

entry-return-6.speaker: COUNSEL
text: Participation is optional.

choice-return.speaker: COUNSEL
text: The code is eight characters. You are still looking at it.

choices.text: I already buy them. Points are points.
You turned every can into a loyalty receipt.
I don't want nicotine purchases gamified.

return-1.speaker: COUNSEL
text: The program is functioning as designed. I have no additional clarification.

return-1-1.speaker: PLAYER
text: That's it?

return-1-2.speaker: COUNSEL
text: That is the complete sentence.

return-2.speaker: COUNSEL
text: That is a fair description. Every code you type in tells the company you bought another one. That is what the points are for. I would rather you hear that from me.

return-3.speaker: COUNSEL
text: Then do not enter the code. The tin works the same without it. Fewer things do, these days.
